sentences.text: A rainbow isn't a stripe painted on the sky. It's sunlight taking a surprisingly complicated detour through rain.
When sunlight enters a water drop, it bends. Different wavelengths, the colors, bend by different amounts.
Light reflects inside the drop, then bends again on the way out. That spreads the sunlight into its colors.
To see a rainbow, the Sun needs to be behind you, with water droplets ahead. Your viewing angle matters.
The full rainbow is actually a circle. From the ground, we usually see only part of it. From a plane, conditions can reveal the whole ring.
A fainter second rainbow comes from light reflecting twice inside the drops. Its color order is reversed.
So, if the rainbow is a circle... have we been chasing the end of something that never had one?
